answer:
Password cracking primarily involves an adversary attempting to guess a password by trying every possible combination until the correct one is found. This method is known as a brute force attack. It is computationally feasible and guarantees success as it systematically goes through all potential passwords based on the character set used (including lower case letters, upper case letters, numbers, and symbols) and the maximum length of the password [Source 1].

Adversaries may employ brute force techniques to access accounts when they do not know the passwords or when they have obtained password hashes. This process can involve systematically guessing passwords using a repetitive or iterative mechanism, often through interaction with a service that verifies the credentials [Source 2]. Additionally, brute forcing can occur at various stages during a breach, leveraging information gathered from other activities such as credential dumping or account discovery [Source 3].
